answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to custody a unique, randomly assigned shard of a shared dataset and answer unpredictable retrieval challenges. A falcon returns to its own nest, and likewise each agent can only prove custody of its own shard; one machine cannot serve many shards at once under time limits, with ferrous bonds locking stake behind each shard, slashed on failed retrieval. The challenge set acts as a prism splitting one claim into many verifiable facets. A thousand fakes then need a thousand shards, stakes, and live servers.
